title: Pages that use localStorage / sessionStorage / document.cookie crash inside the opaque-origin render frame, so whole sections disappear
evidence: robust-localstorage: the original shows 4 habit rows, the date, a '12 day streak' badge and a 7-day grid. The render shows only the static header, the form and an empty 'This week' card ('0 day streak'). The tree has 14 layers. The first `localStorage.theme` read in <head> throws, and so does the `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('habits'))` app script. The runner uses sandbox=allow-scripts, which gives an opaque origin, the same as Figma's null-origin plugin UI that the srcdoc stage inherits. Theme bootstraps, todo/habit apps and React useState(() => localStorage...) are very common in AI-generated apps.
rootCause: ui.html runImport/renderAndExtract. The page runs in a srcdoc iframe that inherits the plugin UI's opaque (null) origin. There, accessing window.localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie or indexedDB throws SecurityError. Nothing shims these before the page's own scripts run, and the agent is appended after </html>, so it runs last anyway.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed independently. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-localstorage`. The original screenshot has the date, "12 day streak", 4 habit rows and a 7-day grid. The render has only the "Habits" title, "0 day streak", the form and an empty "This week" card, at 14 layers. Two scripts throw: the head bootstrap on `localStorage.theme`, and the app script on `localStorage.getItem`. When the app script throws, none of its DOM writes happen. diffPct is only 1.29% because the page is mostly empty background, so the content loss is much worse than the number suggests.

Root cause is in ui.html, runImport/renderAndExtract. The stage iframe has no sandbox attribute and loads via srcdoc, so it inherits the plugin UI's opaque (null) origin. Figma documents that origin; it is also why figma.clientStorage exists. On an opaque origin, the window.localStorage and sessionStorage getters and document.cookie throw SecurityError. Nothing installs fallbacks before the page's own scripts run. The agent (AGENT) is appended after the page, so it cannot help. dev/runner.html (sandbox=allow-scripts) reproduces this faithfully, so this is not a harness artifact.

I tested the proposed fix direction. I wrote a temporary case with an improved shim injected right after <head>, and added `localStorage.theme='light'`, `document.cookie='a=1'` and `history.pushState({},'','/habits')` to the page. The render then matched the original: 57 layers, 22 auto layouts, 0 mock errors. The named-property, cookie and pushState checks all passed. I deleted the temp case afterwards.

The original proposal has three flaws:
(a) A plain object storage breaks named-property access. In the case, `localStorage.theme` reads undefined (harmless there), but `localStorage.theme = 'dark'` followed by `getItem('theme')` returns null. The fix is a Proxy.
(b) A cookie getter that always returns '' makes cookie read-after-write fail. Keep a small jar.
(c) A shim inlined as a UI-only constant never reaches the harness. runner.html extracts only the first <script> of ui.html, so the shim should live in that first script as its own function.

The shim is a no-op on normal origins, because each branch only installs a fallback when the native access throws. It is ES5-style code that runs in the browser iframe, not in code.js, so the ES2017 limit is not affected. No Figma API is involved, so there is no real-Figma API risk.

title: The agent is appended after </html>, so truncated or unbalanced HTML swallows it and the import fails after a 90 s wait
evidence: robust-truncated.html is a normal landing page whose trailing <script> is cut off mid-function, which is common when an AI answer is truncated or copied partially. The browser renders it fine. The harness fails with 'timeout waiting for window.__result'. In the plugin, the user waits 90 s and then sees 'страница не ответила за 90 секунд'. The same happens with an unclosed <style>, <textarea>, <title> or <!-- at the end.
rootCause: ui.html runImport: `renderAndExtract(html + AGENT, ...)`. The agent <script> is string-concatenated at the end. If the page ends inside a raw-text element (script/style/textarea/title) or a comment, the agent markup becomes text or comment, or it merges into the broken script, and never executes. The UI then has no fast way to tell 'agent missing' apart from 'page slow'.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this independently. In ui.html runImport, the agent is added with `renderAndExtract(html + AGENT, ...)`, where AGENT is `<script>(${pageAgent})();<\/script>`. robust-truncated.html ends inside an open `<script>` (cut off mid-callback). The HTML tokenizer treats the agent's `<script>(function pageAgent...` as more text of that unclosed script, until the agent's own `</script>`. The merged block is a syntax error, so the agent never registers its message listener. renderAndExtract then just waits for its 90 s timer. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-truncated` and got `timeout waiting for window.__result`. dev/runner.html appends the agent the same way, so the harness reproduces the plugin's behaviour. This is not a renderer artifact. The same reasoning holds for a trailing unclosed `<style>`, `<textarea>`, `<title>`, `<xmp>` or `<!--`: the agent markup becomes raw text or a comment. A cut-off AI answer is a common way to end up with such HTML, and the failure is total: a 90 s wait, then an unhelpful error.

I checked whether running the agent early is safe. Its top-level code only builds constants, appends the KILL_MOTION `<style>` to `document.head || documentElement`, defines `send`, and calls addEventListener('message'). document.body is read only inside the 'extract' handler, so it can run at the start of `<head>`. SKIP_TAGS already includes STYLE, so the injected style never becomes a layer.

Problems in the proposed fix:
(a) `SHIM` does not exist in ui.html. It comes from some other proposal, and this fix must not depend on it.
(b) "The agent posts 'ready' immediately" races. The agent would run while the head is being parsed, before stage.onload. The UI only adds its message listener after onload, so it would miss 'ready' and always fall into the fallback. The handshake should instead be an ack sent in reply to 'extract'.
(c) The fallback must guard against a double run, or two agents would both answer.
(d) dev/runner.html copies the append logic and would need the same change to keep the harness faithful (that file is off-limits to me).

On the fallback: the stage iframe is a srcdoc iframe with no sandbox attribute, so it inherits the plugin UI's origin. Even an opaque origin counts as the same origin object, so `stage.contentDocument` should be reachable. I could not test this inside real Figma, so the fallback must be wrapped in try/catch and fail fast with a clear error.

title: A CSP <meta> in the pasted page blocks the injected agent (and the injected Tailwind CDN)
evidence: robust-csp.html has `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; ...">`, which pages exported from real sites or frameworks often carry. The page renders fine because it uses only inline styles and Google Fonts. The harness times out ('timeout waiting for window.__result'), and the plugin would show the generic 90 s error.
rootCause: ui.html runImport/renderAndExtract. The page HTML is passed through verbatim. The meta CSP has no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts, so it blocks the agent's inline <script>. It also blocks any Tailwind CDN script the plugin injects.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-csp` and got the same result: "timeout waiting for window.__result" with no tree. In the plugin, runImport sends `html + AGENT` and renderAndExtract puts that into `stage.srcdoc` without changes (ui.html ~L1233-1290). AGENT is an inline `<script>` added at the very end of the document. So the page's `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; ...">` in `<head>` already applies to it, and with no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts the agent never runs. Nothing then answers the `{h2f:'extract'}` postMessage, and the user waits for the generic "страница не ответила за 90 секунд" error. dev/runner.html does the same thing (agent appended after the page), so this is a real plugin bug and not a harness artifact.

Moving the agent ahead of the meta would not be enough on its own. The agent loads images with fetch() (agent ~L981), which falls under connect-src, and here that falls back to default-src 'self'. So images would still fail under such a policy. Removing the meta is the correct fix.

One part of the finding is wrong: the injected Tailwind CDN script itself is not blocked. injectHead puts it right after `<head>`, before the page's meta. A meta CSP only covers content parsed after it, and a parser-blocking script runs before the parser reaches the meta. Also, needsTailwind() returns false for any page with `<style>`, as here. The part that is true: a CSP whose style-src lacks 'unsafe-inline' would block the `<style>` elements Tailwind's runtime adds, and stripping fixes that too.

On severity: AI-generated pages rarely include a CSP meta, but pages saved from real sites or framework builds sometimes do. When it happens the whole import fails after a 90 s hang, so medium is fair.

title: SPAs that render data after mount (fetch/setTimeout) are captured in the loading/skeleton state
evidence: robust-react-cdn (React 18 UMD + Babel standalone + Tailwind play CDN, data arrives 900 ms after mount). The original screenshot shows 7 task cards with avatars. The extracted tree (dev/out/robust-react-cdn.json) has only `div.h-20` skeleton blocks (3 per column, 32 layers) and 0 images. diffPct is only 0.83%, so the harness metric hides it. Every generated React/Vue app with a mocked fetch, a useEffect timer or lazy-loaded data has this problem.
rootCause: ui.html pageAgent settle(). It waits only for document.fonts.ready, the currently present elements and a fixed 300 ms. Nothing detects that the DOM is still changing. Images added by the later render are not awaited, because the list is snapshotted before the render.
fix: In ui.html pageAgent, replace the blind settle() with a wait for pending async work. Install the trackers when the agent script parses, not inside settle(). The agent is appended after , so it parses before DOMContentLoaded. That is before Babel/text-babel, React createRoot, useEffect and most fetch-on-mount code runs. 1) Keep a private timer for the agent itself, before any patching. Change `const sleep = ...` to: const _st0 = window.setTimeout.bind(window); const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => _st0(r, ms)); This is required. Without it, the agent's own sleeps count as pending work and the wait never ends. 2) Add the trackers, right after the KILL_MOTION style is appended: const PEND = { net: 0, timers: new Set(), lastMut: performance.now() }; - setTimeout wrapper: register the id only when 50 <= delay <= 5000. Remove it when the callback fires or clearTimeout is called. Do NOT track setInterval or requestAnimationFrame, because they never finish. - window.fetch wrapper: net++ on call, net-- when the promise settles either way. - XMLHttpRequest.prototype.send wrapper: net++ on send, net-- on 'loadend' (once). - MutationObserver on documentElement {subtree, childList, attributes, characterData} that sets PEND.lastMut = performance.now(). Use plain function wrappers, keep `this`, and pass extra args through. pageAgent runs in the page, not under the ES2017 limit of code.js, but stay conservative anyway. 3) Add quiet(deadline): while (performance.now() < deadline) { busy = PEND.net > 0 || PEND.timers.size > 0 || document.querySelector('[aria-busy="true"]'); if (!busy && performance.now() - PEND.lastMut > 400) return; await sleep(50); } 4) In settle(): call `await quiet(performance.now() + 8000)` first. Then wait for fonts, and only then build the image-pending list. The list is snapshotted after the data render, so the new elements (avatars) are awaited too. The second settle() after the scroll pass catches lazy and reveal-on-scroll content. 5) Optional: also treat a visible '.animate-pulse' or '[class*="skeleton"]' element, or a lone text node matching /^(loading|загрузка)\W*$/i, as busy. This must stay under the same deadline, because some pages ship skeletons permanently. Costs and safety: - A page with a self-rescheduling setTimeout chain (carousel, typewriter, polling) never looks idle and hits the 8 s cap in each settle() call. That is up to about 16 s extra, still well inside the 90 s timeout. - Option to reduce this: ignore timers scheduled from inside a timer callback that the agent is already tracking (chains). - No Figma API is involved, so there is no risk to code.js. Optional hardening: - Timers and fetches scheduled synchronously during HTML parse, before the agent script, are not seen. A tiny tracker
verifierNotes: I re-checked this on my own, and the bug is real. It is worse than reported. 1) Code: ui.html pageAgent settle() (around line 206) only waits for document.fonts.ready, the elements already present (a snapshot), and a flat sleep(300). The 'extract' message handler calls settle(), does the scroll pass, then calls settle() again. Nothing watches for DOM changes, pending timers or network requests. ui.html renderAndExtract appends AGENT at the end of the HTML and posts 'extract' right after iframe onload. dev/runner.html does the same thing. 2) Harness, robust-react-cdn: my rerun got diffPct 1.22, layers 1, images 0. The tree was an empty root frame, so this time even the nav was missing because React had not mounted yet. The original screenshot shows 7 cards with avatars. The reported run (32 layers, skeleton only) is the other side of the same race. The result is flaky from run to run. 3) Timeline: I added a temporary debug copy of the case that logs timestamps into the DOM (removed afterwards). It showed DCL at 2 ms, load at 57 ms, extract message at 76 ms with #root empty, and React mount at 85 ms. The fake fetch resolves about 985 ms in, but extraction had already finished. The extracted texts were only "Sprint 14", "New task", "To do", "In progress" and "Done", with no cards. diffPct (0.8-1.2%) hides this completely, because the skeleton and the empty grey page look almost the same as the original. Problem with the proposed fix: pure MutationObserver quiescence (500 ms idle) cannot see a pending fetch or setTimeout. Those produce no mutations while they wait. React mounts at ~85 ms, then nothing changes until the data arrives. So the idle condition is met long before the data. With the 900 ms case it might pass by accident, because the delays (settle + scroll + second quiet) add up. With a realistic 1.5-2.5 s fetch latency it would still capture the skeleton. There is also a trap in the proposal. If the agent wraps setTimeout, its own sleep() must keep the original setTimeout. Otherwise the agent's own sleeps count as pending work and the wait never ends. I prototyped a corrected fix in a scratch copy of the repo; the repo itself was not changed: - The fix tracks in-flight fetch/XHR and pending one-shot timers (50 ms to 5 s), plus a MutationObserver. - Results: robust-react-cdn went to diffPct 0.02, 75 layers, 26 auto layouts, 7/7 images. A 2200 ms-latency variant (dev/cases/vrf-slowfetch.html, in the scratch copy only) went to diffPct 0.24, 75 layers, 7 images. - landing.html did not regress: 42 layers, 13 auto layouts, 1 image (1 missing), the same as baseline. Its diff was 1.02 vs 2.79 at baseline, which is only image-timing noise between runs.

title: If the Tailwind CDN (injected or page-provided) loads slowly or fails, the page is silently imported completely unstyled
evidence: The first harness run of robust-dashboard (Tailwind v4 browser CDN, on a slow network) extracted a completely unstyled DOM. The aside was a 1424×36 text row, the SVGs had the default 300×150 size and the cards were stacked full-width. Result: diffPct 21.01, heightDelta +887, 684 layers. A rerun with identical HTML gave 1.96 / 0 / 1054 layers. No warning is produced. Tailwind-via-CDN is the most common styling of pasted AI snippets, and the plugin itself injects it.
rootCause: ui.html runImport/needsTailwind/renderAndExtract and pageAgent settle(). The UI proceeds after a 20 s load timeout or when the CDN script errors. The agent never checks whether the utility CSS actually got generated. With @tailwindcss/browser, compilation is asynchronous after the script loads, and settle() does not wait for it.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this by reading the code and reproducing it. In ui.html, runImport() injects `<script src=TAILWIND_CDN>` when needsTailwind() is true. renderAndExtract() then waits for the iframe's onload or a 20 s timer. The agent's settle() waits only for document.fonts.ready, images and 300 ms. Nothing in pageAgent or the UI checks whether utility CSS was ever generated, and no warning path exists. The 'done' handler only reports the layer count and the failed images.

Reproduction: I added dev/cases/robust-verify-twfail.html. It is a Tailwind dashboard snippet whose page-provided script points at a non-existent @tailwindcss/browser@4.99.99, which simulates a CDN outage, being offline or a blocked proxy. The harness ran with 0 mockErrors and extracted 15 layers. dev/out/robust-verify-twfail.render.png shows a fully unstyled document: plain Times text stacked at the top-left, with no sidebar, cards or grid. The plugin would show "Готово: 15 слоёв" with no hint that anything went wrong. Diff and heightDelta are 0 only because the original also failed to load.

A re-run of robust-dashboard gives 1.96 / 0 / 1054, the same as the reporter's second run. So the bad first run was a transient network failure, not a deterministic layout bug. That fits the code path: the CDN script is parser-blocking, so on failure the parser continues with no CSS and the iframe load event fires. In the normal case @tailwindcss/browser compiles in microtasks and MutationObserver callbacks before load, so settle() is enough. The "async compile not awaited" part of the reporter's root cause is therefore minor. The real problem is that no success check exists.

The reporter missed a related flaw in renderAndExtract. If the CDN takes more than 20 s, the timer resolves while the parser is still blocked on the head script. The agent script is appended at the end of the HTML, so its 'message' listener is not registered yet. The 'extract' postMessage is lost, and the import fails after 90 s with "страница не ответила за 90 секунд", a misleading error. The harness runner has no 20 s timer, so it cannot show this.

Severity: medium is right. It depends on the network, but when it happens the import is entirely broken, and Tailwind-via-CDN is the most common styling in pasted AI snippets.

The proposed probe is basically sound, with a few corrections. Gate the probe on an actual Tailwind script or a `style[type=text/tailwindcss]`, not on class-name heuristics. Remove the probe before extract() so it never becomes a layer. Warn rather than abort. Also fix the ready handshake. Bundling Tailwind inline is optional: it adds about 270 KB, pins the version, and does not help pages that bring their own CDN tag.

title: Pasted JSX/TSX components (v0, Claude artifacts) are rendered as raw text with no classes
evidence: Code review. needsTailwind() explicitly matches `class(Name)?=`, which anticipates JSX input. But the browser parses `className="flex ..."` as an unknown attribute 'classname', so no Tailwind class applies. `{items.map(...)}`, `export default function` and `import ... from 'lucide-react'` show up as literal text. v0 and Claude typically output React+Tailwind components, not HTML.
rootCause: ui.html runImport() treats input as HTML only. There is no detection or transformation of JSX/TSX.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed the gap independently. runImport() in ui.html (around line 1233) does only two things to the input: needsTailwind()/injectHead() and renderAndExtract(html + AGENT), which puts the paste into iframe.srcdoc unchanged. Nothing anywhere detects or transforms JSX/TSX. The manifest allows network access to "*", so loading React/Babel from a CDN inside the stage iframe is possible.

I added dev/cases/vrf-jsx-paste.html, a typical v0/Claude TSX pricing component: imports from '@/components/ui/button' and 'lucide-react', export default function, className=, {plans.map(...)}, <Check/>, <Button>. Running `node dev/fidelity.mjs vrf-jsx-paste` produced 16 layers. dev/out/vrf-jsx-paste.render.png shows only literal source text: the import/const/export lines, "{plans.map((p) => (", "{p.name}", "${p.price}/mo", "))}" and so on. There are no cards, no grid and no Tailwind styling. needsTailwind() did match, because `class(Name)?=` accepts className, so Tailwind was injected. It still did nothing, because the HTML parser stores the attribute as 'classname' and the class attribute is never set. <Check/> and <Button> become unknown inline elements. So the result is unusable garbage, not a reduced-fidelity import.

The harness reports diffPct 0, because its "original" side also renders the raw paste. fidelity.mjs cannot measure this gap. That is a limitation of the harness, not evidence that the case works.

Severity is medium, not high. The plugin asks for HTML, and many AI tools can emit full HTML, but React+Tailwind TSX is the default output of v0 and of many Claude artifacts. When that is pasted, the result is completely broken.

The direction of the proposed fix (React UMD + Babel standalone + Tailwind + import stubs) is right, but it has three problems.
(1) The detection regex `className=|export default function|from 'react'|return (<` would misfire on full HTML pages that already contain an inline <script type="text/babel"> React app. The existing dev/cases/robust-react-cdn.html has both className= and `return (<`. Wrapping such a page would break a case that works today. Detection has to require that the input is not an HTML document or snippet.
(2) Babel's transform-modules-umd plus "a regex that strips imports" is fragile. A commonjs transform with a require() shim is the robust option.
(3) The "minimal fallback" of stripping {...} expressions is harmful. It deletes all data-driven content and collapses .map() loops into one item. The fallback should be a clear error message instead.

Also, there is no "DOM-quiescence wait" in the code today; settle() waits only for fonts and images plus 300 ms. So the initial render must be flushed synchronously, not left to rely on timing.

title: The result depends on the user's OS/Figma colour scheme, because prefers-color-scheme in the render frame follows the system
evidence: robust-mobile-shell has a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block. Both the harness original and the extracted tree came out dark (orig.png and render.png show the dark theme) because this Mac is in dark mode. A user in dark mode importing a page designed and reviewed in light mode gets a dark Figma frame, with no way to choose. Tailwind v4's default `dark:` variant uses this media query.
rootCause: ui.html renderAndExtract() has no control over color scheme. The srcdoc stage inherits the host's prefers-color-scheme.
fix:
1) `ui.html` `renderAndExtract()`: before `appendChild(stage)`, set the stage's color-scheme from a new setting `opts.theme` (`'light'` | `'dark'` | `'system'`, default `'light'`, stored with the other settings):
```js
stage.style.colorScheme = opts.theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : opts.theme === 'system' ? 'normal' : 'light';
```
In Chromium (Figma desktop/Electron and Chrome; verified in Chrome 155) the srcdoc document's prefers-color-scheme then follows this value. It applies to CSS @media (including nested Tailwind v4 rules), `matchMedia`, `<link media>`, `<picture><source media>` and cross-origin sheets, with no rewriting. Add the UI select «Тема страницы: светлая / тёмная / как в системе».

2) Fallback in `pageAgent`, used only when the page reports a mismatch: at the start of the extract handler, if `opts.theme !== 'system'` and `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches !== (opts.theme === 'dark')`, rewrite the media rules:
- Walk `document.styleSheets` (wrap `cssRules` access in try/catch for cross-origin sheets) and recurse into every rule that has `.cssRules`: CSSMediaRule, CSSStyleRule (nesting), CSSLayerBlockRule, CSSSupportsRule, CSSContainerRule.
- For each CSSMediaRule, also each `<link rel=stylesheet media>` and each `<source media>`, take the mediaText and substitute only the feature, not the whole query:
  - `/\(\s*prefers-color-scheme\s*:\s*dark\s*\)/gi` becomes `(max-width: 0px)` if the theme is light (always false), or `(min-width: 0px)` if it is dark (always true).
  - The `light` feature gets the opposite substitution.
  
  This keeps `not ...` and `and (min-width:768px)` logic correct.
- Re-run the rewrite from the existing settle/MutationObserver path when new `<style>`/`<link>` nodes appear (Tailwind CDN injects late), then call `settle()` again.

Do not set `colorScheme` on the page's own root element.

3) Harness parity (not part of the plugin): `dev/fidelity.mjs` should screenshot the original with CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia({features:[{name:'prefers-color-scheme', value:'light'}]})`, or `runner.html` should give its iframe `color-scheme:light`, so diffs don't depend on the dev machine's OS theme.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this independently. This Mac is in Dark mode (`defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle` returns Dark). `dev/out/robust-mobile-shell@390.orig.png` shows the dark theme. The extracted tree in `robust-mobile-shell@390.json` has a root fill of rgb(14,14,26), which is the `#0e0e1a` value from the case's `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block.

In `ui.html`, `renderAndExtract()` creates the stage iframe with only width, height and transform. Nothing in `ui.html` mentions color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme, and `settle()` and `extract()` don't touch media rules either. So the srcdoc page picks up whatever color-scheme preference the host has: the OS or browser setting, or Figma's Electron native theme. The same HTML can import light for one user and dark for another, and the user has no control over it. That matters for Tailwind v4 CDN snippets, whose default `dark:` variant uses this media query and which ChatGPT/Claude output often includes.

This is a plugin issue, not a renderer artifact: the extracted tree itself is dark. I kept severity low because most generated pages either don't use prefers-color-scheme or use class-based dark mode. A user in dark mode would also see the page dark in their own browser, so the result is at least consistent with what they previewed.

I tested whether the iframe element's own color-scheme controls this, using the installed Chrome 155 headless:
- Parent page with no color-scheme: the iframe's `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` is true.
- `<iframe style="color-scheme:light">`: false.
- `<iframe style="color-scheme:dark">`: true.
- With `color-scheme:light` on the iframe, a srcdoc `body{background:#fff} @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){body{background:#000}}` computes to rgb(255,255,255). A CSS-nested `.x{ @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){color:blue} }` (the shape Tailwind v4 emits) is also not applied.

So Chromium derives an iframe's preferred color scheme from the embedding element's used color-scheme. That gives a one-line fix that also covers `matchMedia` in JS theme toggles, `<link media>`, `<picture><source media>` and cross-origin stylesheets. The proposed stylesheet-rewriting approach misses all of those.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. Rewriting `rule.media.mediaText` only reaches same-origin `CSSMediaRule`s. It has to recurse into `CSSStyleRule.cssRules`, because Tailwind v4 nests `@media` inside the utility rule within `@layer`. It can't reach cross-origin CDN sheets, `matchMedia`, `<link media=...>` or `<picture><source>`.
2. Replacing a whole compound query with `'not all'` (or `'all'`) gets the logic wrong for `not (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` and for compound queries in dark mode.
3. Setting `document.documentElement.style.colorScheme` inside the page doesn't change prefers-color-scheme at all, and it overrides the page's own color-scheme declaration. It should not be done.

Fix: control the embedder's color-scheme, and keep CSS rewriting only as a fallback for non-Chromium hosts (Figma in Safari/Firefox).

title: The stage iframe and its page keep running after import; page scripts share the plugin UI origin
evidence: Code review. renderAndExtract() removes the previous #stage only at the start of the next import. After an import, the pasted page keeps running behind the UI: carousels, setInterval, videos, WebGL heroes and the decoded image memory. The srcdoc frame is same-origin with the plugin UI and not sandboxed, so page code can touch `parent.document`, post `{pluginMessage:{type:'done'}}` to the UI listener (which does not check e.source), or run frame-busting `top.location = ...`.
rootCause: ui.html renderAndExtract()/the window 'message' listener. There is no cleanup and no sandbox attribute. The UI handler accepts pluginMessage from any source.
verifierNotes:
I checked this by reading the code. No harness case can show it, because dev/runner.html already sandboxes its frame (sandbox="allow-scripts"), so the harness never runs the configuration the real plugin uses.

What the code does now:
- In ui.html, renderAndExtract() removes the old #stage only when the next import starts. After a result, an error or a timeout, the iframe stays in the DOM with its page still running: intervals, carousels, autoplay video and audio that can still be heard, WebGL, and the memory of decoded images.
- The stage gets no sandbox attribute. A srcdoc iframe inherits the origin of the plugin UI, so page code can reach parent.document and parent's functions. Because it shares the UI's realm and event loop, a page alert(), confirm() or busy loop also freezes the plugin UI. Page code can also navigate the frames above it.
- The UI's window 'message' handler (`window.addEventListener('message', ...)` around line 1211) reads e.data.pluginMessage without checking e.source. Even inside a sandbox, the stage can call `parent.postMessage({pluginMessage:{type:'done'}}, '*')`. That would show "Готово" and unlock the UI while code.js is still building.
- The channel between the agent and the UI is already safe. onMessage checks `e.source === stage.contentWindow`, and the agent checks `e.source === parent`.

Is sandbox="allow-scripts" safe for the plugin's features?
- Yes. The Figma plugin UI already has a null origin. That means localStorage and cookies already throw, and fetches already send Origin: null. A sandboxed frame without allow-same-origin keeps the same behavior for fetch with CORS, Google Fonts, createImageBitmap and canvas toBlob. The imageBytes()/toPng() paths behave the same, and canvas tainting rules don't change.
- postMessage between the agent and the UI keeps working, because both checks compare contentWindow and parent by object identity.
- Modals are suppressed, which fixes the alert-freezes-UI case.
- Navigating the top frame and opening popups are blocked.
- The harness already validates this exact configuration.

Removing the stage after extraction is also safe. The result, including the image bytes, has already been structured-cloned into the UI before the 'import' message is posted, and nothing reads the stage after that.

One part of the proposed fix is risky: accepting a pluginMessage only when `e.source === parent`. Figma delivers figma.ui.postMessage from its host window, and I am not confident that this window is always `window.parent` of the UI document in every Figma client (web, desktop, wrapper iframes). If it isn't, the guard would drop the real settings, progress, done and error messages and break the plugin. The safer guard is the negative one: drop messages that come from the stage.

verifierNotes:
I confirmed this by reading the code and testing the regex in node; I did not run the full harness. In ui.html, needsTailwind() at line ~1260 bails out with `if (/<style|stylesheet|tailwind/i.test(html)) return false;`, which tests the raw HTML. The same regex is copied in dev/runner.html (line 20) and dev/fidelity.mjs (line 116).

I took dev/cases/media-tw-icons.html, removed its explicit CDN <script>, and ran it through the current function. It returns false, so Tailwind is not injected and the page renders unstyled. The only thing blocking it is the comment "Tailwind UI style icons". With the corrected check it returns true.

It is wider than comments. Any visible text containing "Tailwind" or "stylesheet" also blocks injection, for example a dev-tool landing page that says "Built with Tailwind CSS" (I tested this: old=false, new=true). That is plausible on AI-generated pages, but most AI output either includes the CDN script or uses <style>, so the impact stays low/medium. I'm keeping it at low.

- `\b` on the tag names
- a link `rel` that may come after `href`

- `<link href=a.css rel=stylesheet>`
- `<script src=https://cdn.tailwindcss.com>`
- `<style type=text/tailwindcss>`

There is no Figma API involvement and no ES2017 concern, because this code runs in the UI iframe.

title: Image fetches have no timeout, so one slow remote image stalls the whole import until the 90 s error
evidence: The first run of layout-grid-stacking (9 picsum.photos images; curl showed 11-18 s per image and some failing) produced 'timeout waiting for window.__result': no tree at all. The same case with data: images finishes in about 45 s. In the real plugin this shows 'страница не ответила за 90 секунд' and imports nothing.
rootCause: ui.html loadImages()/imageBytes(): `await fetch(url)` has no AbortController. settle() only bounds load events (8 s), not the agent's own fetches.
verifierNotes: I checked this independently and the gap is real. In ui.html, imageBytes() calls `await fetch(url)` with no signal and no timer. loadImages() runs 6 workers and has no overall deadline. settle() only waits up to 5 s for fonts and up to 8 s for load/error events; it puts no bound on the agent's own fetches. The only backstop is renderAndExtract's absolute 90 s timer ('страница не ответила за 90 секунд'), and when it fires the import produces nothing. The cited case (layout-grid-stacking) now uses data: images, so re-running it proves nothing. I wrote a deterministic repro instead (scratchpad stall.mjs). It is a local server whose /stall.png never responds. The is inserted after the load event so the runner's frame.onload is not blocked. That matches the real UI, which proceeds after its 20 s onload timeout anyway. The page also has one normal image. Results: - Original ui.html: no __result after 120 s, so the real plugin would hit the 90 s error. - A copy of ui.html with only the AbortController change in imageBytes: result in 29 s, with the rest of the tree intact. The server log also showed something the finding missed. The second request for the stalled URL only reached the network about 17 s after the first, at about 20.8 s. Chrome's HTTP cache lock makes fetch() wait on the in-flight request for the same URL. So even a slow image that does finish costs about 20 s of cache-lock wait plus download, per worker slot. The abort timer, which starts when fetch() is called, covers that wait too. The proposed fix is correct in direction but needs two details: 1. The timer must cover res.blob() as well, because a stalled body hangs too. Clear it only after the body has been read. 2. A per-image timeout alone does not bound the total. Many slow images run 6 at a time, plus up to about 27 s of settle() time, can still pass 90 s. An overall deadline is needed. Nothing is lost when bytes come back null: imageBytes already falls back to the decoded (if complete), and code.js prepareImages then tries figma.createImageAsync(url), with a placeholder fill as the last resort. A related point at lower risk: prepareImages awaits createImageAsync one image at a time, so many slow URLs make the Figma side slow, but it is not cut off by the 90 s timer.

title: Network-bound image loading has no per-image timeout and runs inside the 90 s global deadline, so one slow asset fails the whole import
evidence: Measured on this machine: an 11 MB unsplash original (w=6000) took 45.6 s to download, and picsum fetches added ~30 s in robust-dashboard (progress 'Загружаю картинки 1/9' at 10.0 s, '2/9' at 40.6 s). The first harness runs of robust-dashboard and robust-mobile-shell timed out completely. In the plugin, the page load can use up to 20 s, then settle() 5+8 s, then loadImages() refetches every image with no timeout. On a slow connection the 90 s renderAndExtract timer fires and the already-measured layout is thrown away.
rootCause: ui.html loadImages()/imageBytes(): `await fetch(url)` with no AbortController. renderAndExtract(): a fixed 90 s timer that does not reset on progress. code.js prepareImages() awaits figma.createImageAsync(url) serially, also with no timeout, and the UI stays locked meanwhile, with no watchdog for the main-thread phase.
verifierNotes: I checked the code and the claims hold. In ui.html, imageBytes() calls `await fetch(url)` with no signal or timeout. loadImages() runs 6 workers with no overall budget. renderAndExtract() arms a fixed 90 s timer (`setTimeout(() => done(new Error('страница не ответила за 90 секунд')), 90000)`) that 'progress' messages never reset. When it fires, the measured tree is thrown away, even though extract() already finished and only image bytes were still pending. Before that timer even starts, the agent spends up to 20 s on the iframe load wait plus two settle() calls (up to about 13.3 s each), so less than 60 s is left for images. In code.js, prepareImages() awaits figma.createImageAsync(url) one image at a time with no timeout, for every image whose bytes came back null. A fetch that stalls on a hung connection never resolves on its own (no browser-level timeout for minutes), so one bad asset kills the whole import. Harness check: my robust-dashboard run collided with a parallel agent (an ENOENT on a shared temp file), so it proves nothing. robust-mobile-shell passed in 46 s on a warm network (diff 1.62 %, 11 images, 0 missing). The timeout therefore depends on the network and does not reproduce reliably. curl showed picsum taking 2-5.7 s for 2 KB files on this machine, which supports the reporter's slow-network measurements. The bug comes from the code path, not the renderer. Problems with the proposed fix: 1. "Prefer reusing the decoded via canvas" is wrong as the first choice. Page elements have no crossorigin attribute, so cross-origin images taint the canvas (toPng throws). Re-encoding a photo as PNG also inflates the payload several times compared with the original JPEG/WebP. And `el` is null for CSS background images. Keep it as the fallback, as the code does now. 2. A per-image timeout alone doesn't fit the budget. With 6 workers and 15 s each, 30 images can still take 75 s. 3. When fetch times out and bytes is null, code.js currently retries the same slow URL through createImageAsync. That just moves the hang to the main thread. 4. The UI watchdog that unlocks after 60 s without messages would misfire. buildNode() is synchronous and posts no progress, so a big tree can block the main thread for a long time. The UI would then unlock mid-build and allow a second import to start.

title: Large or WebP images are re-encoded to PNG at up to 4096px no matter how small they are displayed, giving huge payloads
evidence: robust-mobile-shell@390: a 122 KB WebP background (unsplash fm=webp&w=1600) arrives as a 1,158,241-byte PNG, 9.5× larger. robust-dashboard with a w=4200 JPEG (1.4 MB) shown as a 36×36 avatar: the agent's result grew to 21,359,943 bytes of JSON (measured via a scratch copy of the runner), because the image was re-encoded as a ~4096×2340 PNG. The harness then hung for more than 7 minutes on that payload. AI pages often use raw unsplash URLs without a w= parameter (5000–6000px originals) and 'fm=webp/auto=format'. Each such image becomes a 15–30 MB PNG, cloned twice (iframe→UI→main thread) and decoded by Figma.
rootCause: ui.html imageBytes(). (a) sniff() recognizes only PNG/JPEG/GIF, so WebP/AVIF always go through toPng(). (b) Any JPEG/PNG wider than 4096 goes through toPng() at 4096px. The displayed size (el.getBoundingClientRect() and background box) is never considered. (c) It always encodes PNG, even for opaque photos. (d) The ImageBitmap from createImageBitmap is never .close()d, so decoded bitmaps (~100 MB for a 6000×4000 photo) stay until GC.
verifierNotes:
I checked this against the code and it holds up. ui.html imageBytes() only passes the original bytes through when sniff() recognises PNG, JPEG or GIF AND both dimensions are 4096 px or less. Every other image goes through toPng(), which always writes 'image/png' at up to 4096 px. imageRef() never records the size the image is displayed at, so a 36 px avatar gets the same treatment as a hero image. The ImageBitmap is never closed.

What I measured:
(1) robust-mobile-shell@390.json, img10: the 122,024-byte image/webp from fm=webp&w=1600 arrives as base64 of length 1,544,324, which is about 1.16 MB of PNG. This matches the finding.
(2) The raw Unsplash URL photo-1554224155 with no parameters is a 5563x3192 JPEG of 1.56 MB. Scaled to 4096 and saved as PNG with sips it is 9.68 MB. Avatar photo-1500648767791 raw is 3000x4499 and 4.2 MB; as a 4096 PNG it is 18.9 MB.
(3) A one-image case I wrote (that raw URL shown at 40x40) made dev/fidelity.mjs hang. I killed it after 400 s with no output. A control case using ?w=400 finished in 76 s, but its image came back missing (imagesMissing=1, bytes null). So this harness run had network trouble, and the hang alone does not prove the payload caused it. The byte sizes above stand on their own without it.
I deleted both temporary cases so a full harness run won't hang on them.

Corrections to the finding:
- 'auto=format' does NOT trigger this. fetch() sends Accept: */* and Unsplash then returns image/jpeg (checked with curl: 192 KB JPEG). Only an explicit fm=webp/avif or a .webp/.avif file goes through the PNG path.
- The main cost is speed, memory and payload, not how the result looks. In Figma the images still come out right, just slowly and with a lot of memory; several raw images on one page could hit plugin memory limits. So medium, not high.
- The proposed target formula max(dispW, dispH)*2 is wrong for cover/FILL. Example: a 5563x3192 image in a 40x40 cover box needs a short side of 80 px (2x), but the formula caps the long side at 80, giving a short side of about 46 (only 1.15x).
- A 16x16 alpha check can miss transparency, because low-quality bilinear downscaling skips pixels.
- 'or <= 4096' in the pass-through rule is ambiguous.
- Transferring buffers only helps on the iframe-to-UI hop. Plugin UI to main-thread messages go through Figma, so a transfer list does nothing there.

title: Scroll containers in app-shell layouts (h-screen + overflow-y-auto) import only the first viewport; the rest is hidden behind clipsContent
evidence: robust-mobile-shell@390: `.app{height:100vh}` > `.scroll{flex:1;overflow-y:auto}` becomes the frame 'div.scroll' with h=776 and clip=true, while its children extend to y=1096. The Netflix/Apple/Starbucks rows and the promo card exist in the tree but are invisible in Figma, and the root is 844 tall. The same applies to Tailwind dashboards using `h-screen overflow-hidden` with `<main class="overflow-y-auto">`, the most common generated dashboard shell. The pre-extraction scroll pass also scrolls only window, so lazy content in the inner scroller never triggers.
rootCause: ui.html extract()/docHeight() measure only document scroll height. walk()/boxVisual() faithfully record overflow clipping. Nothing expands inner scroll containers or scrolls them.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-mobile-shell -w 390` and got diffPct 4.64 and heightDelta 0. The harness viewport is 390x900 (the plugin's mobile preset is 390x844). The tree has root 390x900 > div.app 390x900 > `div.scroll` at y=68, h=832, clip=true, with 12 children. Their y values run to 936+160=1096: the tx rows at y 852 and 936 and the whole promo card sit below the 832 clip. In the render PNG the list stops at Netflix behind the tab bar, so Apple, Starbucks and the promo are hidden. The pixel diff cannot show this, because the original screenshot is also viewport-only. The evidence is the JSON geometry plus the code.

The root cause is as reported. In ui.html, the message handler's scroll pass and extract() both rely on docHeight(), which reads only documentElement/body scrollHeight. walk() and boxVisual() record overflow as `clip` (line 379). Nothing un-scrolls inner scrollers. The import is technically faithful to the browser viewport. But on normal pages the plugin imports the full page, and app-shell pages (h-screen / 100vh + overflow-y-auto, the standard v0/Claude dashboard and mobile shell) lose most of their content. That gap is real for "transfer everything".

Problems in the proposed fix:
(1) `style.flex='none'` on the scroller breaks the most common dashboard shape, `flex h-screen` (row) > `main.flex-1.overflow-y-auto`: main would shrink to its content width. Only reset flex in a column-direction flex parent.
(2) Matching "computed height == innerHeight" misses calc(100vh-64px), dvh, h-full chains and grid rows. It is more robust to unlock every ancestor up to html and use the old rect height as min-height.
(3) Scrollers inside position:fixed containers (fixed sidebars, modals, drawers) cannot grow the document and must be skipped.
(4) Scrolling each inner scroller is redundant once they are expanded before the scroll pass. Do it only when the option is off.
(5) The fixed-bottom re-anchoring must subtract the parent offset `oy` and should apply only when expansion happened.
(6) dev/fidelity.mjs screenshots the original without expansion, so the harness would report a large heightDelta. The harness needs the same pre-pass (harness work, not a plugin bug).

Overall this is a UX/semantics gap, not a broken render. Medium severity is fair.

title: Visually-hidden (Tailwind 'sr-only') content leaks as visible text, and an sr-only native checkbox gets a synthetic 1px box
evidence: gen-tw-controls.render.png: the close button shows '✕Close panel' overflowing the card edge. gen-tw-controls.json has TEXT 'Close panel' 84.66x24 ABS inside button.rounded-md, from <span class='sr-only'> (position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip:rect(0,0,0,0)). The Flowbite toggle's <input class='peer sr-only'> becomes FRAME input[checkbox] at -1,11.5 1x1. Because !v.has, formNode paints the synthetic white fill and gray stroke on it. The sr-only pattern is in practically every Tailwind/shadcn/Flowbite icon button, toggle and file upload.
rootCause: ui.html walk(): the isTextBlock/blockText branch runs before the 'collapsed wrapper' size check, and blockText measures the text's range rects, which overflow the 1x1 clipped box. Neither cs.clip (rect(0px,0px,0px,0px)) nor clip-path:inset(50%) is checked, and a 1×1 box with overflow:hidden is not treated as invisible. formNode then synthesizes visible paint for checkboxes with no own styling.
verifierNotes:
I reproduced this independently. Running `node dev/fidelity.mjs gen-tw-controls` gave diffPct 0.62 with 0 mockErrors. In dev/out/gen-tw-controls.json the button.rounded-md frame holds a TEXT 'Close panel' at 17,7 sized 84.66x24 with absolute=true. In render.png the "✕Close pane" text runs past the right edge of the card. Both Flowbite toggles become FRAME input[checkbox] at -1,11.5 sized 1x1. One has a synthetic blue fill and the other a white fill, and both get a gray 1px stroke.

Root cause, checked in ui.html:
- walk() only checks display, visibility and opacity before the tag switch, so INPUT goes straight to formNode().
- formNode() paints a synthetic box because `!v.has`.
- For the <span class=sr-only>, isTextBlock(span) is true, and blockText → textGeometry measures the Range rects. With nowrap the text overflows the 1x1 clipped box, and visual.has is false, so the bare TEXT is returned outside the box.
- The "collapsed wrapper" check (box.w<0.5) never runs, and even if it did a 1x1 box would not trigger it. Nothing reads cs.clip or cs.clipPath.

This is not a renderer artifact: real Figma would get the same overflowing TEXT layer and the same painted 1x1 frame. The pattern appears in most Tailwind UI, shadcn and Flowbite icon buttons, toggles, close buttons and file inputs (it is also in robust-dashboard.html).

Corrections to the proposed fix:
(1) The regex `/inset\(\s*50%/` is too loose. `inset(50% 0 0 0)` only clips the top half and would wrongly hide visible content. The clip/inset values need to be parsed into a real zero-area test.
(2) The `clip:rect(0,0,0,0)`-only regex misses other common hidden rects such as WordPress `.screen-reader-text`, which uses `rect(1px,1px,1px,1px)`.
(3) The claim that hidden text is merged into paragraphs via gatherRuns does not hold today. isTextBlock already returns false for any child with position absolute/fixed, and sr-only is absolute, so a parent with an sr-only child is never a text block. The visible effect of that path is a different one: the parent loses single-layer styled-text merging, and the span leaks through childrenOf → walk.
(4) If isTextBlock is changed to skip hidden children, textGeometry() and lineCount() must also leave those children out. Both call range.selectNodeContents(el), so the hidden span's overflowing nowrap rects would widen R or add lines and break width and alignment detection. Changing isTextBlock/gatherRuns alone would cause a regression.

The core walk()-level early return is safe. It runs before the tag switch, so the INPUT never reaches formNode. It only removes nodes that paint nothing in the browser (clip and clip-path apply only to positioned elements, or remove all paint), and it uses no Figma API.

title: sr-only / visually-hidden text becomes visible full-width text layers
evidence: robust-dashboard: `
rootCause: ui.html walk(). For an element where isTextBlock() is true and visual.has is false, `return [t]` emits the bare text node. The element's own overflow clip (visual.clip), its tiny 1×1 box and CSS `clip`/`clip-path` are all ignored. textGeometry() measures the Range rects, which extend far beyond the 1px box because of white-space:nowrap.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs robust-dashboard`: diffPct 1.96, 0 mock errors. The finding holds.

1) sr-only text. dev/out/robust-dashboard.json has a TEXT node "View notifications" (x=17, y=7, 134.39×24, absolute:true) inside `header.sticky > button.relative` (36×36). The `if (!visual.has) return [t]` branch then emits the bare text and drops visual.clip, which is true for overflow:hidden. Nothing in walk() looks at the 1×1 rect, `clip` or `clip-path`. textGeometry() uses Range client rects, and with white-space:nowrap they span the full 134px string.

The non-text path already handles this (`plain = !visual.has && !(visual.clip && overflows)` keeps a clipping frame). Only the text-block branch has the gap.

2) truncate cells. `td.truncate` emails are bare TEXT nodes, 451.72px wide at x=286 in the row. In the render they run over the Plan column ("…customer-account-0Starterenterprise-example-domain.com"). The original shows "olivia.martin.customer-…". Same root cause. - Skipping visually hidden elements is correct. It is better placed before the tag switch, so `<input class="sr-only peer">` (common in Tailwind toggles and radios) is skipped too, instead of becoming a 1×1 formNode.
- The 1×1 + overflow heuristic covers several variants: Tailwind v3 (clip rect(0,0,0,0)), Tailwind v4 (clip-path inset(50%)), Bootstrap .visually-hidden, and WordPress .screen-reader-text (clip rect(1px,1px,1px,1px)). Matching only `rect(0px, 0px, 0px, 0px)` would miss the WordPress variant.

- The clip-frame wrapping is safe with auto layout. fitLayout() returns null when a child overflows (`end < -T`), so the wrapper stays a fixed-size frame with clipsContent and never becomes a hugging frame that grows to the text width.

title: Closed <details> content is rendered (FAQ answers leak below and overlap the next items)

That text sits outside the frame, and gen-forms.diff.png shows a solid red 'Yes.' under 'Can I cancel anytime?' at about y=647, sitting on the hr. Root cause is in ui.html. walk() (lines 277-285) only skips nodes with display:none, visibility other than visible, or opacity 0. isTextBlock's scan (line 643) and gatherRuns (line 682) only check display:none.

- Closed details > p: computed display is block and the rect is a real 740x18, but checkVisibility() is false. An inline span shows the same pattern.
- Open details > p: checkVisibility() is true.

Separately, the summary's disclosure ::marker triangle is also missing from the render. That is a separate, minor gap.
